findings.text: `.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs:6` now has a static `import { check } from "./jsonl-schema.mjs"`. If that file ever fails to load (a syntax slip, a bad merge), ledger.mjs can't even start, and every task log goes silent with nothing reporting it. Before this change ledger.mjs didn't depend on that file at all, so this breaks the owner's top rule ("nothing here may make ledger.mjs go silent"). The try/catch around `check()` can't catch a failed import. A simple fix: `let check = () => null; try { ({ check } = await import("./jsonl-schema.mjs")); } catch {}` (the file already uses top-level await).

`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js:3` has the same static import. If jsonl-schema.mjs breaks, the dev server can't boot, not just append. That fails loudly, so it is less serious than item 1, but the same dynamic import with a fallback would make the two files behave the same way.

`.claude/hooks/jsonl-guard.mjs:47` reads `tool_input.file_path`, but NotebookEdit sends `notebook_path`. So the NotebookEdit part of the matcher never blocks anything, and the test at `jsonl-guard.test.mjs:91` passes only because it hand-builds a `file_path`. This is harmless in practice (nobody edits a .jsonl as a notebook), but the test claims more than the hook does. Read `file_path ?? notebook_path`, or drop NotebookEdit from the matcher.

The earlier review's notes 2, 3 and 5 are all fixed in this diff: `is_main()` now matches on the filename (`ledger.mjs:286`), Append.js wraps `check()` in try/catch (`Append.js:450`), and the test cleans up with try/finally. Append.test.mjs still writes under `public/` without `hold.mjs`, so each run still fires a reload.

I re-checked every browser caller of `rpc:append` against the new check, and they all still pass. `ai2/inbox.js:405,416` writes `card` lines with an `id` to board.jsonl. `ext/AITask/decisions.js:187` writes `verdict` lines with `id` and `decision` to task.jsonl. `day-audit` and `v/3` write to files with no schema. One catch: inbox.js swallows any reply with `.catch(() => null)`, so if a card line is ever refused, it will vanish without a word.

The `"unchecked"` key that ledger adds sits beside the verb. The task.jsonl reader (`ext/JSONL/JSONL.js:137` `apply()`) merges a stray key like that into the verb's object, so readers don't break. It only matters if something ever re-checks old lines.

The diff carries task-dir noise: `review/diff.patch` contains an older copy of itself, and `files.jsonl` lists `requirements.md` three times. The main checkout also has many unrelated `files.jsonl` changes and a modified `.claude/skills/clarity/flags.jsonl` (`git status`). Keep all of these out of the merge.

findings.text: All five items are done as asked, and all four test files pass when I ran them in the worktree: jsonl-guard 24/24, jsonl-schema 38/38, ledger 5/5, Append 8/8. I also recomputed the flags.jsonl schema myself: 173 lines, all with `at`, `target` and `verdict`, and the same seven verdict values. That matches `.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs:80-91` exactly.

`.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs:282`: the new `is_main()` check means the hook runs only when `import.meta.url` exactly matches `process.argv[1]`. If the two ever differ, the whole ledger goes silent and nothing reports it. That is exactly what the owner's top rule forbids. They could differ if the repo is reached through a junction or symlink, because Node resolves the real path. I tried upper-case and lower-case drive letters and backslash paths, and all of them matched. A sturdier check is `/ledger\.mjs$/i.test(process.argv[1] ?? "")`, or moving `append_checked` into its own small module so ledger.mjs needs no guard at all.

`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js:67`: `check()` has no try/catch here. If it throws because of a bug in the checker itself, the batch is not written and the browser gets back the generic "Append failed" error. The owner's rule says a check that throws on its own bug should log and let the line through, as ledger.mjs already does. Wrapping the call the same way would make it consistent.

`.claude/hooks/ledger.mjs:214` adds `"unchecked"` as a top-level key beside the verb, as the brief asked. If anything ever re-checks a task.jsonl line written this way, `check()` will call `"unchecked"` an unknown verb. append.mjs never re-judges old lines, so nothing breaks today.

`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.test.mjs:479` writes its scratch files into `public/framework/ai/_append-test-tmp/`, inside the live site. Each run fires live reloads, and a test that crashes partway leaves the folder behind. Running it under `node Server/hold.mjs on`, or wrapping the body in try/finally, would avoid both.

I checked the browser code that calls `rpc:append` and none of it is affected by the new check. `public/layouts/browse/verdicts.js` and Dictate's `prompts.jsonl` write to files with no schema, and ContentModule writes to page.jsonl, whose schema is open. The worktree also has many unrelated files.jsonl files modified (`git status`), so make sure none of them end up in the merge.
